02 · HOW TO COMMUNICATE WITH CLAUDE
The Three S's
Simple principles to stay on track.
⌕
Situation
what & why
What are you actually trying to do? One sentence of framing before the ask.
☷
Specific examples
paste it
Reference files with @, paste the real error log. Don't describe what you could show.
✓
Success criteria
definition of done
What does finished look like? Tests pass, tsc clean, the page renders.

7. What is Context?
03 · CONTEXT
Every Turn Carries the Whole Conversation
Fix the login redirect
Edited Login.tsx
Now add a test
re-reads turns 1-2
Added Login.test.tsx
Actually, revert that
re-reads turns 1-4
Removed Login.test.tsx
The entire transcript is re-sent
EVERY SINGLE TURN
and all of it fills up your context window...
Managing it is your job, not the model's.

9. What is the Context Window?
03 · CONTEXT
Too Much Context
Turn 1
Turn 2
Turn 3
Turn 4
Turn 5
Turn 6
Turn N
?
Nobody fails at turn two.
You don't fail because the task got harder.
You fail because there's too much to hold.
≣
Contradictory information
Lots of detail in the window, some of it no longer true.
↺
Abandoned approaches
Old attempts still sitting in memory, competing with the current one.
⚠
Hallucinations and mistakes
Small errors creep in, and they compound as the session runs on.
⌫
Costs effort to clear
You now pay to get the memory back to something clean.
10
10. Too Much Context
03 · CONTEXT
Too Little Context
Like a vague bug report is not helpful, so too is a vague prompt.
unhelpful
It doesn't work.
Page doesn't look right.
Can you fix the thing?
✗
No steps to reproduce
Nothing to run, so nothing can be confirmed before a fix is attempted.
⚠
Unclear expected vs outcome
No way to tell whether the change worked or only looked like it did.
⌕
Need to ask questions and investigate
The work starts with a hunt for the information you already had.
And now you're making Claude do its own investigation — which leads to wasted tokens, wasted time...

04 · CONTEXT MANAGEMENT
Chat Functions
Simple commands to master your chat sessions.
⌫
Clear
/clear
Moving to a new task? Start a new chat and fresh context.
↺
Rewind
/rewind or double-esc
Unhappy with a result? Go down the wrong path? Rewind instead of re-prompt.
↻
Resume
/resume
Cleared too soon? Resume a previous session.
⤓
Compact
/compact <what_to_keep>
Running out of context but still need to continue the work?

04 · CONTEXT MANAGEMENT
Effort Is the Second Dial
How much thinking the model spends before it answers — set independently of the model.
low
medium
high
xhigh
effortLevel: medium
⚡
Two pairings worth knowing
Sonnet + medium is the everyday default. Opus + low gets you the stronger model without paying for deliberation you don't need.

16. Effort Is the Second Dial
04 · CONTEXT MANAGEMENT
Plan First and Save Tokens
Plan: Fix the Flaky Checkout Test
Read first
src/checkout/CheckoutForm.tsx
tests/checkout.e2e.ts (3 failures)
1. Await the /cart response instead
of the 500ms timeout
2. Seed the cart via API in beforeEach
3. Re-run the suite 10x to confirm
Files: 1 source, 1 test
Verify: pnpm test:e2e --repeat 10
Not doing: the wider timeout cleanup
⌕
It gathers first
Forces Claude to read and investigate before proposing anything.
☷
You review the plan
The work is described before it is done. Redirect while that is cheap.
⚡
It saves tokens
Catching a wrong direction in a plan costs far less than in a diff.
Opus + plan mode
Switch to Sonnet to run.

05 · CLAUDE CUSTOMIZATION
Your Setup Loads Context for You
▤

at session start
Map of the project, key commands, gotchas. Global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md loads in every project.
◎
MEMORY.md
auto-managed
Claude's own notes, kept per project.
⚑
Rules
on matching paths
Path-scoped guidance in .claude/rules/.
⚙
Skills
on matching task
Repeatable workflows, by slash or by match.
Session start
CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md
You open a file
matching rules
You name a task
matching skill
Mid-task

19. Your Setup Loads Context for You
05 · CLAUDE CUSTOMIZATION
CLAUDE.md — The Project Map
CLAUDE.md
# Payments API
## Commands
pnpm dev # local, needs Docker up
pnpm test:int # integration, slow
## Architecture
- Routes in src/routes, thin.
- Business logic in src/domain.
- Never call Stripe outside
src/domain/billing.
## Gotchas
- Migrations are NOT auto-run.
- CI uses Node 20, not 22.
/init
Drafts a project-level CLAUDE.md from the codebase. Always edit what it produces.
•
Architecture notes
•
Build, test, deploy commands
•
Gotchas that bite newcomers
•
Links to external docs
•
Keep it short — it loads every time
20
20. CLAUDE.md — The Project Map
05 · CLAUDE CUSTOMIZATION
Rules Load When They Apply
Guardrails for reading and writing in specific files and folders.
.claude/rules/dotnet.md
---
paths: ["**/*.cs"]
---
- Async methods end in Async.
- No LINQ in hot paths.
- xUnit, not NUnit.
.claude/rules/react.md
---
paths: ["src/**/*.tsx"]
---
- Function components only.
- Co-locate tests as *.test.tsx.
- No default exports.
⚡
Path-scoped beats always-on — your C# conventions cost zero context on a TypeScript day.
Rules without a path scope always load like a CLAUDE.md.
21
21. Rules Load When They Apply
05 · CLAUDE CUSTOMIZATION
Skills are Recipes for Repeated Work
SKILL.md
---
name: pr-description
description: Write the PR
description for a branch. Use
when asked to open a PR or
write a PR body.
---
1. Diff the branch against main.
2. Group changes by intent.
3. Fill the PR template.
4. List anything needing review.
A skill can be a simple list of steps, a branching workflow, or a full instruction book with scripts attached.
Invoke implicitly
•
Description does the triggering
•
Claude picks it up by matching
Invoke explicitly with /
•
Name the skill yourself: /pr-description

30. Pro-Tips
07 · PRO-TIPS
Ask Me Questions
Tell Claude to ask you questions to help you solidify your idea.
your prompt
I want to add a saved-reports
page to the admin app.
Ask Me Clarifying Questions
Who can see a saved report?
❯ 1. Any signed-in user
2. Admins only
3. Only the person who saved it
Where do reports get stored?
1. A new reports table
❯ 2. Reuse reports + a saved flag
“
Start with an idea
A half-formed idea that needs some iteration.
☼
Claude Asks You
What you actually mean, what is in and out of scope, what done looks like.
✓
End specific
A fleshed-out plan, concrete enough to hand straight to plan mode.
⚙
The /brainstorming and /grill-me skills run this loop for you.

31. Ask Me Questions
07 · PRO-TIPS
Debug Loop
A disciplined loop for hard bugs and performance regressions.
diagnose
/diagnose When I run
<insert_command> I get this
error <error_log> - list top
3 causes and suggest a fix
⌕
Describe the Issue
What you did, what broke.
☷
Paste a Log
The real error text, not a summary.
✓
Expected vs Actual
What should have happened, and what happened instead.
⚙
/diagnose
Great for troubleshooting bugs or cryptic errors.

07 · PRO-TIPS
Adversarial Review
Normal review — getting a check-up with your primary doctor.
Adversarial review — getting a second opinion.
adversarial review
Review @my-plan.md looking
for high-value criticism
> 3 assumptions that do not
> survive contact
> 1 cheaper alternative
✗
Critical Eye
Criticizes instead of agreeing.
☼
Fresh Perspective
Approaches without prior knowledge.
⌕
Reduces Bias
Sees outside the context of the original session.
⚙
/adversarial-review
Runs the second opinion for you, on a plan or a diff.
